screening_decisions.reason: Prospective diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4, CA125, ROMA, and RMI (which combine menopausal status, ultrasound, and biomarkers) in patients with pelvic mass, using histology as reference standard. Meets inclusion criteria.
Prospective cross-sectional study assessing HE4, CA125, and ROMA in women with pelvic mass; histopathology used as reference. Directly relevant to combinations of biomarkers and menopausal status.

Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study (prospectively collected data) validating the ADNEX model (incorporates age, CA125, ultrasound features) in adnexal mass patients, with histopathological reference. Evaluates a combination model.

Retrospective audit of CA125 usage in clinical practice, not a diagnostic test accuracy study. Does not evaluate a combination of tests against a reference standard for ovarian cancer diagnosis in women with pelvic mass.

Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study (prospectively collected data) externally validating ADNEX and comparing with RMI and other ultrasound methods in adnexal mass patients, using pathology as reference. Includes combination models.
Systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study (cross-sectional or randomised trial). Does not meet the inclusion criteria for study designs.
Evaluates the predictive value of various RMIs (combining ultrasound, CA125, menopausal status) in adnexal mass patients with histopathology as endpoint. Diagnostic accuracy study meeting criteria.
Prospective multicenter study comparing HE4, CA125, and ROMA in women with benign pelvic mass and ovarian cancer, with histology as reference. Evaluates combinations incorporating menopausal status.

Diagnostic accuracy study comparing HE4, CA125, and ROMA in patients with gynaecological diseases including ovarian cancer; histological confirmation used. ROMA combines biomarkers and menopausal status.

Systematic review on symptoms associated with ovarian cancer diagnosis, not a diagnostic accuracy study of test combinations. No evaluation of menopausal status, ultrasound, or biomarkers as index tests.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of HE4, CA125, ROMA. Not a primary diagnostic accuracy study; secondary research does not meet inclusion criteria.
Global cancer statistics epidemiological report. Not a diagnostic test accuracy study; does not evaluate any index test for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

Prospective multicenter diagnostic study developing and validating the ADNEX model (combines age, CA125, ultrasound predictors) in women with adnexal mass, using histology as reference. Directly relevant.

Retrospective study comparing CA-125, HE4, ROMA, and RMI-II in women with adnexal masses and histological diagnosis. Evaluates combination algorithms incorporating menopausal status, ultrasound, and biomarkers.

Explicitly described as a case-control study, not a cross-sectional design. Inclusion criteria specify cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy studies or randomised trials. Study design does not match.

Primary study evaluating HE4 and ROMA in women with benign ovarian cysts, endometriosis, and EOC, with histological confirmation. Evaluates combination algorithm (ROMA) incorporating menopausal status.

Prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study (IOTA3) comparing various ultrasound-based strategies and RMI in women with adnexal masses; histology as reference. Evaluates combinations including menopausal status.

Original development paper for RMI, combining CA125, ultrasound, and menopausal status in women with pelvic masses. Diagnostic accuracy study with histological reference; foundational combination model.
Immunohistochemistry and basic science study of HE4 protein expression in ovarian tissues. Not a diagnostic test accuracy study; does not evaluate test performance in women with pelvic mass.
Diagnostic accuracy study comparing CA125, HE4, and ROMA in women with ovarian masses, using pathologic examination as reference. Evaluates combination index incorporating menopausal status.

Prospective study evaluating HE4, CA-125, and ROMA in women with suspicious cystic ovarian masses scheduled for surgery, with histology as reference. Assesses combination of biomarkers and menopausal status.
Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating CA125, HE4, and ROMA index in benign gynecological diseases and ovarian cancer, with histological confirmation. ROMA combines biomarkers and menopausal status.

Prospective validation of simple ultrasound rules and comparison with RMI and logistic regression models in adnexal masses. Although simple rules use only ultrasound, the study compares them against combination models (RMI includes CA125 and menopausal status). Meets inclusion criteria.

Observational diagnostic accuracy study evaluating ROMA (combination of HE4, CA125 and menopausal status) in 260 postmenopausal women with ovarian masses, using histopathological verification as reference standard. Meets inclusion criteria: cross-sectional DTA study of a test combination for ovarian cancer diagnosis in symptomatic women with pelvic mass.

This is a population-based modelling study projecting future cancer incidence and mortality; it is not a diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating tests for ovarian cancer diagnosis, nor does it involve women with pelvic masses or compare tests. Excluded as not meeting DTA study design.

Qualitative interview study describing women's perspectives on the diagnostic process; does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy of tests or test combinations, and lacks a reference standard. Not a DTA study, excluded.

Narrative review/overview of ovarian cancer biology and molecular genetics; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study and does not evaluate test combinations against a reference standard in women with pelvic masses.

Nested case-control study evaluating prediagnostic biomarker trajectories in trial participants, not a cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study in women presenting with a pelvic mass. Does not evaluate test combinations with ultrasound or menopausal status for diagnostic accuracy.

Methodological paper describing a quality assessment tool for systematic reviews; not a primary study evaluating diagnostic accuracy of tests for ovarian cancer, and does not involve patients or a reference standard.

Diagnostic accuracy study validating ROMA (a multivariable algorithm combining CA125, HE4 and menopausal status) in 207 women with a pelvic mass, with definitive histologic diagnosis as reference standard. Fits cross-sectional DTA design evaluating a test combination.
Literature review of CA125, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Does not present original data evaluating test combinations or compare tests in women with pelvic masses.
Review and hypothesis paper proposing a model of ovarian tumorigenesis; not a diagnostic accuracy study, no evaluation of test combinations for diagnosis, no reference standard.
Critical review of proteomic techniques, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Does not report original test accuracy data for a defined population with pelvic masses.

Cross-sectional study evaluating the Risk of Malignancy Index (RMI, a combination of ultrasound findings, CA125 and menopausal status) in 540 women with adnexal masses, with histopathological diagnosis as reference. Reports accuracy separately for pre- and postmenopausal women. Meets inclusion criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study of ROMA (combining HE4, CA125 and menopausal status) in 443 patients with a pelvic mass, using biopsy or clinical follow-up with imaging as reference standard. Directly evaluates a test combination for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

Retrospective/prospective study comparing diagnostic accuracy of expert sonography, CA125, RMI and their combinations in 1362 women with adnexal masses, with histopathology as reference. Evaluates test combinations and reports accuracy stratified by menopausal status. Fits DTA study design.

Prospective multicenter cross-sectional study validating IOTA ultrasound-based strategy (simple descriptors + simple rules) in 1165 women with adnexal masses, with surgical histology as reference. Although the index test is primarily USS, the review includes single tests that are components of combinations, and this study compares with RMI. It meets inclusion criteria as a DTA study in the target population.
Simulation study evaluating statistical methods for meta-analysis; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. No patient data, no index test or reference standard for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4, CA125 and ROMA (algorithm incorporating menopausal status) in 756 patients with pelvic masses, with histological confirmation of diagnosis. Proposes optimized cut-offs for early-stage detection. Meets inclusion as a cross-sectional DTA study of test combinations.

External validation of the ADNEX multivariable risk model (including clinical and ultrasound predictors) for differential diagnosis of adnexal tumors in surgical cohorts, using histology as reference. This is a model validation DTA study, fitting the inclusion criterion 'studies validating multivariable models for the diagnosis of OC'.

Cohort study evaluating the impact of implementing symptom-triggered referral pathways on cancer outcomes (stage shift, referral patterns), not a diagnostic test accuracy study. Does not assess accuracy of test combinations against a reference standard.

Multicenter prospective study validating a predictive model combining HE4, CA125 and menopausal status (separate algorithms for pre/post) to classify malignancy risk in 531 women with a pelvic mass, using surgical histology as reference. Fits inclusion criteria as a validation of a test combination model for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

Clinical practice guideline providing recommendations for management of adnexal masses; not a primary study presenting original diagnostic accuracy data. No test evaluation against a reference standard in a defined patient cohort.

Molecular genetic study investigating somatic mutations in ovarian cancer subtypes; does not evaluate diagnostic test accuracy or test combinations for ovarian cancer diagnosis. No reference standard for diagnostic accuracy.

Incomplete abstract suggests a brief review/opinion piece comparing HE4 with CA125; lacks evidence of a primary diagnostic accuracy study design with a well-defined patient cohort, index test and reference standard. No quantitative test accuracy data reported in the abstract.

Prospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4 and ROMA (combination of HE4, CA125, menopausal status) in 414 Asian women with a pelvic mass, with surgical histopathology as reference. Reports accuracy separately for pre- and postmenopausal women. Meets inclusion criteria.
Not a diagnostic test accuracy study; reports incidence trends, not evaluating ultrasound or biomarker tests for ovarian cancer diagnosis.
This is a systematic review, not a primary cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study or randomised trial; does not meet inclusion criteria.
Prospective diagnostic accuracy study evaluating ROMA (combination of biomarkers and menopausal status) in women with adnexal masses, with histopathology reference.

Cross-sectional study validating ultrasound-based prediction models (IOTA LR2, SR, RMI) incorporating ultrasound features and biomarkers, with histology reference; includes menopausal status stratification.
This is a meta-analysis, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study; does not meet inclusion criteria.
Prospective cross-sectional study evaluating biomarkers and risk models (ROMA, RMI) in women with ovarian lesions, compared to histopathological diagnosis.
Multicenter diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA in women with suspicious pelvic masses, against histological diagnosis.
Methodological paper on meta-analysis techniques; not a primary study evaluating diagnostic tests for ovarian cancer.
Methodological simulation study on meta-analysis methods; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study for ovarian cancer.
Study on germline mutations and genetic predisposition; not a diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating ultrasound or biomarkers for ovarian cancer diagnosis in symptomatic women.
This is a review article, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.
Prospective multicenter blinded trial validating ROMA (combining HE4, CA125, menopausal status) in women with adnexal mass, using histology reference.
Prospective study evaluating four RMI versions (incorporating ultrasound, CA125, menopausal status) in women with pelvic masses, with histopathology reference.
Diagnostic study assessing RMI and CA-125 in postmenopausal women with adnexal masses, compared to surgical histology.
Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4, CA125, ROMA in women with benign ovarian diseases vs epithelial ovarian cancer, stratified by menopausal status.
Case-control study focused on symptoms for early detection; does not evaluate ultrasound or biomarker tests for diagnosis in women with a pelvic mass.
Prospective validation study of ROMA (HE4+CA125+menopausal status) in women with a pelvic mass scheduled for surgery, using histology as reference.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Diagnostic accuracy study comparing biomarkers and risk models (ROMA, RMI) in women with ovarian masses, with histopathological confirmation.
This is a clinical guidance statement on genetic risk assessment, not a diagnostic test accuracy study for ovarian cancer.
Cross-sectional study evaluating CA125, HE4, ROMA in women with ovarian masses, using postoperative histopathology as reference.
Diagnostic study evaluating HE4, CA125, ROMA in postmenopausal women with ovarian tumors, with histological confirmation.
Evaluates ultrasound (2D, 3DPD) and CA125, along with RMI, IOTA models in postmenopausal women with ovarian tumors, compared to histopathology; assesses diagnostic accuracy.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study enrolling 129 patients with pelvic mass(es) suspicious for ovarian cancer. Evaluates single biomarkers (HE4, CA125) and a combination (ROMA) that incorporates menopausal status, with histological reference standard.

Prospective diagnostic accuracy study in women with complex pelvic masses (n=50). Compares HE4, CA125, ROMA (includes menopausal status) and RMI (includes USS, CA125, menopausal status). Reference standard is surgery/histology.
Describes a tool for risk of bias assessment of prediction model studies; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.

Diagnostic study evaluating ROMA, HE4, and CA125 in 104 women with pelvic mass (plus 49 healthy controls). Analysis focuses on pre- and postmenopausal subgroups. Reference standard is surgical histology.
Study on routes to cancer diagnosis using administrative data; does not evaluate diagnostic test accuracy.
Methodology paper on bivariate meta-analysis; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.

Prospective population-based diagnostic study enrolling 901 women with a pelvic mass scheduled for surgery. Directly compares RMI and ROMA (both combine menopausal status with biomarkers/USS). Histological reference standard.
Software macro/user guide for meta-analysis; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Meta-analysis of primary studies; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.

Diagnostic accuracy study using a multicenter database of 2445 patients with adnexal masses. Evaluates IOTA ultrasound-based logistic regression models and RMI (which includes menopausal status, USS, and CA125). Histological reference standard.

Subset analysis of a prospective trial evaluating HE4 and CA125 for detection of epithelial ovarian cancer in 229 premenopausal women with an adnexal mass. Reference standard is surgery/histology. Meets criteria for single test evaluation in the target population, specifically in a menopausal subgroup of interest.

Focuses on prediction, therapy monitoring, and prognosis; does not clearly define the control group as women with pelvic mass suspicious for OC. Not a cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study in the target population.

Reports only biomarker levels in women with benign gynecological disorders (prior to surgery for pelvic mass). Does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity/specificity) for discriminating malignant from benign disease; no malignant cases are compared.
Narrative review article; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.

Likely a case-control study using healthy controls or controls without pelvic mass; does not specify enrollment of women with a pelvic mass suspicious for ovarian cancer. Fails to meet the population criterion.
Systematic review of prediction models; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Study is on endometrial cancer, not ovarian cancer. Does not meet the condition criterion (ovarian cancer diagnosis).
Meta-analysis; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating CA125, HE4, and ROMA in 762 women with benign gynecological disease and 70 with ovarian cancer (indicating presence of pelvic mass). Histological reference standard. Meets criteria for single tests and test combination (ROMA includes menopausal status).
This is a review of diagnostic indices; it does not present primary diagnostic accuracy study data.

Multicenter prospective diagnostic trial enrolling 638 women with an unknown ovarian cyst or pelvic tumor. Validates HE4, CA125, ROMA, and RMI (all relevant test combinations). Histological reference standard.

Primary study validating the ADNEX model, a multivariable model that combines ultrasound features and CA125 (biomarker) for differentiating adnexal masses. Histological reference standard. Meets criteria for studies validating prediction models investigating test combinations.
